messages.subject: Re: NBLAST
parts:
Dear Charles,

Thanks for your interest NBLAST. I'm sorry I was unable to reply to your
initial message immediately and it then disappeared over my email
horizon.

If you want to make sure that you have everything you need for complex
analysis, try running:

https://gist.github.com/jefferis/bbaf5d53353b3944c090

You could try running some of the figures from the original NBLAST paper
e.g.

https://github.com/jefferislab/NBLAST_figures
https://github.com/jefferislab/NBLAST_figures/blob/master/fig/Auditory_neurons/FullAudInterneuronAnalysis.Rmd

This is somewhat demanding test that everything is working. I also
recommend taking a look at the "nat-user" google group and using that to
make any future queries on specific topics.

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google
group since the answer may be of interest to others.

--
Gregory Jefferis, PhD
Division of Neurobiology
MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
Francis Crick Avenue
Cambridge Biomedical Campus
Cambridge, CB2 OQH, UK

http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/h-to-m/g-jefferis
http://jefferislab.org
http://flybrain.stanford.edu


On 8 Oct 2018, at 22:22, Charles Danziger wrote:

> Hello Dr. Jefferis,
>
> My name is Charles Danziger and I am an undergraduate at Yale
> University
> working in Dr. James Jeanne's lab. I have been reading about your work
> with
> NBLAST and have found it incredibly powerful. I am trying to map a few
> areas of the brain using your programs and was wondering if you had
> any
> suggestions about a good place to start. I have been testing my
> computer by
> running your demo codes and everything seems to be going well so far.
> I am
> just curious if there is a good way to ease myself into the data
> analysis
> to make sense of what your programs are able to compete in terms of
> mapping
> connections in the brain.
>
> Any help would be very much appreciated.
>
> All the best,
>
> C. Danziger
